question: The length of the common tangent PQ for two circles touching externally is 16 cm. If the radius (OP) of the bigger circle is 20 cm, then the radius (RQ) of the smaller circle is:
solution:
Given:

Radius (R) = 20 cm

radius (r) = r cm

Formula Used:

Length of common tangent = 2√(R × r)

R & r are radii

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/826319999c5f4e16fc66a7a3a20bc9658969782ca2521559e75da6d5d8146c13.png] 

Solution:

Length of common tangent = 2√(20 cm × r cm)

16 = 2√(20r cm²)

On squaring both the sides:

r = 64/20 cm

= 3.2 cm.

Therefore, the length of the radius of the other circle is 3.2 cm.
